summary: Lambert Schmithausen is an Indologist and philosopher working in Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Erich Frauwallner (~1958-1963) and studied with Paul Hacker (~1963-1966), later serving as associate professor at the University of Münster (1970-1973).

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at McMaster University by 1986 and later served as a professor at the University of San Diego (attested 1997).

Lance S. Cousins worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and K. R. Norman. He lectured at the University of Manchester (~1970-2000) and taught at the University of Oxford (~2000-2015).
Lang Chen works in Buddhist and religious studies. Chen earned a PhD at Yale University under doctoral supervisors Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff, and also studied under Janet Gyatso.

Lang Eun Ra is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Ra pursued doctoral studies at Temple University under supervisor Charles Wei-hsun Fu, also studying with Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

Lara Braitstein specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned a PhD at McGill University, where she studied under Richard P. Hayes and later became an associate professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism (attested 2026).
Laren Hogen Bays specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Having studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada, Bays founded and served as co-abbot of Great Vow Zen Monastery.

Larry DeVries is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Minnesota. DeVries taught at Minnesota, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the University of Washington, and was later affiliated with Langara College (attested 2005).

Lars Fogelin works in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a PhD at the University of Michigan (1995-2003) under Carla M. Sinopoli and held posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University, and the University of Arizona.

Lars Martin Fosse is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and computational fields. He studied at the University of Oslo, Heidelberg University, and the University of Bonn, later teaching at the University of Oslo (attested 2002).

Lata Chhatre works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Chhatre has held posts at Savitribai Phule Pune University, serving as a Reader in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2009) and as Visiting Faculty (attested 2026).

Lati Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar who studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and Gyume Tantric College. He served as abbot of Ganden and Ganden Shartse monasteries (~1976-1985) and was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1976.

Latika Lahiri was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Xianlin Ji at Peking University as an Indian Government scholar in 1958 and held a post at the University of Delhi (~1969-1988).

Laura Harrington is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under teachers including Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi, Gary A. Tubb, Lobsang Jamspal, Kirti Rinpoche, Nathaniel Dickson, and Gregory A. Hillis.

Lauran R. Hartley is a Tibetologist who held teaching posts at Indiana University Bloomington and Rutgers University (attested 2003). She later became an adjunct assistant professor and Modern Tibetan Studies Program director at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Laurence Austine Waddell was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a medical degree from the University of Glasgow. He served as a military medical officer (~1880-1917) and later became Professor of Tibetan at University College London (1906-1908).

Laurence Binyon worked in art history, Sinology, and Japanology after studying at Trinity College, Oxford (~1888-1892). He held long-term posts at the British Museum (~1893-1933) and later at Harvard University (~1933-1934).

Lauri Karttunen was a computational linguist who completed his doctorate at Indiana University Bloomington under Fred Householder (~1965-1969). He held long-term appointments at the University of Texas at Austin, the Palo Alto Research Center, and Stanford University.

Laurie L. Patton works in Indology and religious studies, earning a PhD at the University of Chicago (~1984-1991). She held posts at Emory University, Duke University, and served as president of Middlebury College (2015-2024).

Lavanya V. Eswar is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. As of 2026, Eswar is attested as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.
